turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Before you say anything else, tell me who decided that, and on what basis.
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.

"That's the end of it." A machine's guess, and the company that sells it printed that it should never be the sole basis for punishing a student; I have their guide in my bag. Your own procedure, 4.3, says software alone does not establish anything, so either withdraw the zero or I'm in the principal's office at 4:40.
I don't need more proof than that.

"I don't need more proof than that." I'm writing that down, word for word. Was Owen heard before that zero went in, yes or no, because when we're done here I'm walking straight to the principal's office, and that sentence goes with me.
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.
My child never lies. "Unlike some people." Are you calling Owen a liar, or me, because either way that sentence is going upstairs with me today.

Then put it in writing tonight: who decided, on what basis, and whether anything is on Owen's record right now. I'm asking the principal to review this today, and if that goes nowhere, it goes to the board under section 42. You still haven't told me whether you spoke to Owen before you entered that zero.
